A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dualformer and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G. Retained and relocated material can be matched reliably, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original Maze and Sokoban experiments, math-model fine-tuning results, ablations, and qualitative examples in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds analyses of automatic mode use and generalization to different maze densities and shapes.

M1.justification: The architectures, four structured trace-dropping levels, randomized training, plan/create control tokens, and math reasoning-step dropping remain unchanged. The new experiments evaluate the existing method.

E1.justification: Section 5.1.4 adds Maze test scenarios with out-of-distribution wall densities of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.6, plus six rectangular sizes evaluated using a model trained on 20×20 mazes. The original Maze, Sokoban, and math coverage remains.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Solution-Only, Complete-Trace, bootstrapped Searchformer, Mix-p variants, and the math fine-tuning baselines. Appendix G retains o1-preview and o1-mini. The new generalization tests evaluate Dualformer alone; newly cited works are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds fixed-density testing reported as 50 unseen mazes per case and rectangular-maze testing. Its new auto-mode diagnostic measures the slow-mode fraction among feasible outputs using 64 responses on 1,000 mazes. Existing training settings and benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Sections 5.1.3–5.1.4 substantially extend the analysis beyond the existing dropping/mixing ablations and examples: they investigate difficulty-related mode use and robustness to wall-density and maze-shape shifts. These introduce previously untested behavioral questions and expose generalization failures.

E5.justification: No repeated-training-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests are added. The new analyses retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Existing comparative scores are unchanged. New Tables 5.5–5.6 report 0% solved at densities 0.1 and 0.2, 68% optimal/72% solved at 0.6, and rectangular-maze optimal rates of 73–100%. New Figure 5.1 reports a generally increasing slow-mode share among feasible paths with density and maze size. These are additional-condition findings, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of trace dropping, its categorical distribution, and the SWC metric are unchanged. No formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: one controllable fast/slow/auto model, improved planning performance and efficiency, greater solution diversity, and application to math fine-tuning. The new analyses provide evidence and qualifications without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly discusses density-specific generalization limits and speculates that short prompts explain low-density failure. It also offers two explanations for increased slow-mode representation on harder mazes: successful solutions may require slower reasoning, or the model may select slow mode more frequently.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code availability statement and repository link on page 1. The architecture, hyperparameters, data-generation details, and prompts documented in the appendices remain unchanged. Repository availability itself was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds SwiftSage (Lin et al., 2023) and DART-Math (Tong et al., 2025), extending the single-model contrast to SwiftSage. It removes the cognitive-science related-work paragraph and its Povey, Thaler/Sunstein, and Tversky/Kahneman references. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Most wording and section order are retained. Changes include paragraph splitting, limited wording edits, a new generalization subsection, removal of the cognitive-science paragraph, and shortened Mix-p discussion with updated cross-references.

P2.justification: v2 adds the mode-use Figure 5.1 and generalization Tables 5.5–5.6. The original Mix-p Figure 5.1 moves unchanged to Figure D.1. Several main-text tables are enlarged and repositioned; existing appendix illustrations and result displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical transparency by exposing previously unreported generalization failures and investigating mode use, while adding code-access information. The gains are limited: mode-use statistics condition on feasible paths, and the stated 50-case density evaluation leaves Table 5.5's 97% entry unexplained. The core method and comparative results remain unchanged.
